messages.subject: Effectiveness of a Combiner
messages.body_plain:
Is a combiner effective at all times? I am running the following code where you can see that I am using part-m-00001 (single map file) for testing.  I am testing this in two different instances. One with the combiner and other without. And the one without the combiner is actually faster. I am trying to understand why that is so. Is it because the data set is small, and for  Combiner to be effective the data must be large?

======================================================
##################################################
#
##################################################
library(Rhipe
rhinit()
rhclean()
#ifolder <- rhls("/user/totaldb",recurse=T)$file
ifolder <- "/user/totaldb/1401/2299/part-m-00001"
ofolder <- "/user/nooftimes.ing.ed"

t2r <- list()
t2r$map <- expression({
        lapply(map.values,function(r){
                add.tmp.df <- r[complete.cases(r[c(2,4,5)]) & grepl(".+\\.\\w+-*\\w*\\.\\w+\\.\\w+",unlist(r['qname'])),]

                apply(add.tmp.df,1,function(s){
                        ad.yes <- ifelse(s['qtype'] == 'address',1,0)
                        bk.yes <- ifelse(1 %in% unlist(s[7:17]),1,0)
                        rhcollect(s['source'],list(1,ad.yes,bk.yes,0,0))
                        qd.add <- gsub("(\\d+)\\.(\\d+)\\.(\\d+)\\.(\\d+)\\.\\w+-*\\w*\\.\\w+\\.\\w+","\\4\\.\\3\\.\\2\\.\\1",s['qname'])
                        rhcollect(qd.add,list(0,0,0,1,bk.yes))
                })

        })
})

t2r$reduce <- expression(

pre = {
                final.list <- list()
        },
reduce = {

                final.list <- append(final.list,reduce.values)

        },
post = {

                tot.qr <- sum(unlist(lapply(reduce.values,function(t){t[[1]]})))
                tot.aq <http://tot.aq> <- sum(unlist(lapply(reduce.values,function(t){t[[2]]})))
                tot.bk <- sum(unlist(lapply(reduce.values,function(t){t[[3]]})))
                tot.qd <- sum(unlist(lapply(reduce.values,function(t){t[[4]]})))
                tot.qb <- sum(unlist(lapply(reduce.values,function(t){t[[5]]})))
                rhcollect(reduce.key,list(tot.qr,tot.aq <http://tot.aq>,tot.bk,tot.qd,tot.qb))
        }
)
t2r$input <- ifolder
t2r$output <- ofolder
t2r$mapred <- list(mapred.task.timeout = 0
#                , mapred.reduce.tasks = n
                , mapred.reduce.slowstart.completed.maps = 0.80
)
t2r$readback <- FALSE
t2r$combiner <- TRUE
t2r$mon.sec <- Inf
t2r$jobname <- t2r$output
t2r.watch <- do.call("rhwatch", t2r)
rhclean()

======================================================

Thanks, Ashrith

messages.subject: Re: Install Rhipe 0.66 failed on Ubuntu11.10 32bit
messages.body_plain:
Sanal, are you running Ubuntu?

If you have a root access can you run "sudo updatedb" and then run "locate protobuf.pc" ? If you don't see anything then protobuf.pc is not installed.

 If you see protobuf.pc  and it is not in /usr/lib/pkgconfig/proto* then you will have to add the base directory to PKG_CONFIG_PATH

Also, you seem to have installed protobuf without sudo (unless you did the entire installation as root), in that case protobuf would not get installed and you will have to do it again with a sudo.

Also can you check if you have set $prefix?

Regards, Ashrith
